business_model.claim: APA is an independent energy company whose subsidiaries explore for, develop, and produce crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs.
quotes: APA Corporation (APA or the Company) is an independent energy company that owns subsidiaries that explore for, develop, and produce crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P5 (10-Q MD&A, filed 2026-08-10)
business_model.claim: APA's producing operations span three geographic reporting areas—U.S., Egypt, and the North Sea—with active development offshore Suriname targeting first production in 2028.
quotes: The Company's business has oil and gas operations in three geographic areas: the U.S., Egypt, and offshore the U.K. in the North Sea (North Sea).
is currently progressing with an oil field development offshore Suriname targeting first production in 2028

business_model.claim: U.S. crude oil is marketed to integrated major oil companies, marketing and transportation companies, and refiners, priced on WTI-based indices with 30-day evergreen contracts.
quotes: APA primarily markets its U.S. crude oil production to integrated major oil companies, marketing and transportation companies, and refiners based on West Texas Intermediate (WTI) pricing indices

business_model.claim: U.S. natural gas is sold to local distribution, utility, and midstream companies, end-users, marketers, and integrated major oil companies at liquid index sales points.
quotes: Natural gas is sold to a variety of customers that include local distribution, utility, and midstream companies, as well as end-users, marketers, and integrated major oil companies.

business_model.claim: In Egypt, substantially all natural gas production is sold to EGPC under a gas sales agreement effective January 2025, with a minimum realized price of $2.65 per MMBtu.
quotes: Effective January 2025, substantially all of the Company's natural gas production was sold to EGPC under the terms of this agreement.
the gas sales agreement that establishes pricing based on a minimum realized price of $2.65 per MMBtu

business_model.claim: The Egypt MCA imposes a fixed 40 percent cost recovery limit and a fixed profit-sharing rate of 30 percent for all production under the concession.
quotes: The consolidated concession has a single cost recovery pool to provide improved access to cost recovery, a fixed 40 percent cost recovery limit, and a fixed profit-sharing rate of 30 percent for all the Company's production covered under the concession.

business_model.claim: North Sea natural gas is sold to a third party at the St. Fergus entry point of the national grid on a National Balancing Point index price basis.
quotes: The gas is sold to a third party at the St. Fergus entry point of the national grid on a National Balancing Point index price basis.

business_model.basis: stated in P1 (10-K Item 1) and P3 (10-K MD&A)
business_model.claim: APA purchases third-party natural gas and crude oil to fulfill long-term delivery commitments, generating a trading margin; in 2025 purchased oil and gas sales were $1.7 billion against associated purchase costs of $1.1 billion.
quotes: In order to satisfy certain delivery commitments, the Company purchases third-party natural gas and crude oil to sell and deliver under existing pipeline agreements and sales contracts.

Sales related to purchased volumes increased $150 million for the year ended December 31, 2025 to $1.7 billion from $1.5 billion in 2024. Purchased oil and gas sales were partially offset by associated purchase costs of $1.1 billion and $1.0 billion for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively.

business_model.claim: APA's long-term delivery commitments require an average of 152 Bcf of natural gas per year from 2026 through 2029, 49 Bcf per year from 2030 through 2037, and 1.8 MMbbls of crude oil per year from 2026 through 2028.
quotes: The Company has long-term delivery commitments for natural gas and crude oil that require APA to deliver an average of 152 Bcf of natural gas per year for the period from 2026 through 2029, an average of 49 Bcf of natural gas per year for the period from 2030 through 2037, an average of 1.8 MMbbls of crude oil per year for the period from 2026 through 2028

business_model.claim: Revenue is driven primarily by commodity prices and production volumes; in 2025 total oil and gas production revenues were $7,229 (table in millions) with average realized crude oil prices of $66.92 per barrel.
quotes: Crude oil prices realized in 2025 averaged $66.92 per barrel.

business_model.claim: In Q2 2026, average realized crude oil prices surged to $98.24 per barrel, a 50 percent increase over Q2 2025, driving a $688 million increase in oil revenues.
quotes: Crude oil prices realized during the second quarter of 2026 averaged $98.24 per barrel
A 50 percent increase in average realized prices increased second-quarter 2026 oil revenues by $688 million compared to the second quarter of 2025

business_model.claim: Lease operating expenses (LOE) are the largest operating cost, comprising direct operating costs, repairs and maintenance, and workover costs, and trend with commodity prices and production type.
quotes: LOE includes several key components, such as direct operating costs, repairs and maintenance, and workover costs. Direct operating costs generally trend with commodity prices and are impacted by the type of commodity produced and the location of properties.

business_model.claim: Depreciation, depletion, and amortization (DD&A) is a major non-cash expense tied to production volumes and reserve estimates; in 2025 the oil and gas property DD&A rate was $13.41 per boe.
quotes: The Company's oil and gas property DD&A rate remained relatively flat in 2025 compared to 2024, from $13.44 per boe to $13.41 per boe

business_model.claim: U.S. producing assets are primarily in the Permian Basin (Midland and Delaware sub-basins), where APA holds approximately 2.6 million gross acres and operated roughly 4,000 gross wells in 2025.
quotes: APA has access to significant liquid hydrocarbons across its 2.6 million gross acres (1.3 million net acres) in the U.S..
The Company operates approximately 4,000 gross oil and gas wells across its acreage

competitive_position.claim: Commodity price volatility is a primary threat: the 10-K notes that APA's revenues, operating results, growth rate, and carrying value of oil and gas properties depend highly upon realized prices, and sustained low prices could impair the company's ability to fund capital expenditures, replace reserves, and return capital to shareholders.

Sustained low prices of crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs could also further adversely impact the Company's business, including by weakening the Company's financial condition and reducing its liquidity, limiting its ability to fund planned capital expenditures and operations, causing the Company to delay or postpone some of its capital projects or reallocate capital to different regions, limiting the Company's access to sources of capital, such as equity and long-term debt, or reducing the carrying value of the Company's oil and gas properties, resulting in additional non-cash impairments.
